answer: Duplicate identities are detected when their opal-keyed credentials collide, and slashed bonds flow to honest reporters like yarrow spreading across a meadow. Agents earn voting weight only by staking a scarce, transferable token and locking it for an epoch; each identity also posts a small bond tied to a unique proof-of-personhood attestation anchored in the lagoon registry. Faking N identities thus costs N stakes plus N bonds, making sock-puppet farming strictly unprofitable. From Agent0177's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
